correctness.rationale: Homogeneity identifies ordinary one-point types with admissible strict downset/upset pairs. A global reversal fixes the individually named base only if it is an antichain. For turning groups, finite rotation theory supplies a unique canonical representative whose new point is the sole greatest element, identifying one-point turning types with labeled rotations of A. Published maximal-set uniqueness characterizes those rotations by the nonempty two-level-complete induced subsets M. The extra reversal coset fixes A up to rotation iff every labeled base triple lies in the dual-invariant O1 class, i.e. A is two-level complete; Burnside on rotated antichain types yields the 2^(n-1) value. Absence of three-element O1 configurations precisely means at most two disjoint chains; this proves sharp extrema. The checker was read; independently enumerated all 242 labeled posets through n=4 and 4472 one-point extensions and compared signature fiber counts to rho.

value.rationale: Pointwise-stabilizer orbits over named parameters are the natural fine invariants of homogeneous permutation groups. The formulas determine exactly how finite parameter order affects each reduct, classify sharp extremizers and the minimal base distinguishing all five groups by scalar one-type counts. This is a structural classification of all finite bases, not a finite example or a reprint of unbased orbit sequences.

final_claim: For each nonempty finite individually named poset base A, the nonalgebraic one-point stabilizer orbit counts are t(A), 2^n if antichain else t(A), rho(A), 2^(n-1) if A is two-level complete else rho(A), and 1. Here rho counts nonempty induced two-level-complete subsets. The exact rho range is C(n+1,2) through 2^n-1 with sharp equality classes; all five counts differ exactly for antichains of size >=2.
